answer_raw:
The answer depends on whether you are looking at consumer-grade workstations or the massive-scale clusters used by frontier AI labs.

## The Current Hardware Landscape

For high-end desktop/workstation use, the **RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition** is described by NVIDIA as the most powerful desktop GPU ever created, per a September 2026 report [3].

In the realm of massive-scale AI infrastructure, the "most powerful" hardware is shifting between NVIDIA's GPU ecosystem and Google's specialized hardware. While NVIDIA has historically been the default choice for both training and inference due to its CUDA ecosystem [1], Google's newer **Ironwood TPU** has significantly closed the performance gap for inference workloads [2]. 

| Hardware Type | Leading Model/System | Primary Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Desktop GPU** | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition [3] | Professional workstations / local compute |
| **AI Accelerator** | Google TPU (e.g., Ironwood) [2] | Large-scale cloud inference and training [1] |

## What Claude and Others Are Using

Anthropic's compute strategy relies heavily on a strategic partnership with Google.

**Anthropic** — The company uses a combination of GPU and TPU clusters to train, scale, and deploy its AI systems [4]. Under its Google Cloud partnership, Anthropic has access to up to **5 GW of next-generation TPU capacity**, a deal intended to massively expand its compute infrastructure for frontier Claude models [8].

**Others** — Most enterprise-level users have traditionally defaulted to NVIDIA GPUs for their versatility in both training and inference [1]. However, as of April 2026, Google began selling its own specialized TPUs directly to external customers, offering a specialized alternative to the NVIDIA-only standard [1]. For developers looking for single-accelerator performance, Google's **Gemma 3** is positioned as a top-tier model for running on a single GPU [5].
